steps.work:
1. GET /l/{token} resolves a share link — arriving with no traveller in hand, through the global unique index on token — and answers docs/PUBLIC-ENVELOPE.md's allowlist and nothing else. Unauthenticated, rate-limited, and the capability kept out of the log.
2. **THE REDACTION IS ONE FUNCTION AND FOUR CALL SITES GO THROUGH IT** (PD-08). v7.0 wrote 'the path is REDACTED from the log' — singular — and touched neither middleware.go nor ratelimit.go. Measured on the running container: `curl /l/CAPABILITY7XY` logs `"path":"/l/CAPABILITY7XY"`. Four sites print `r.URL.Path` and the attribute redactor decides on the attribute KEY, which here is `path`, so it can never fire. `httpx.LoggedPath(r)` rewrites `/l/{anything}` to `/l/[redacted]` and AccessLog, Recover, RateLimit and logFailure all call it. **The rate limiter's line is the sharp one**: it fires precisely when somebody is enumerating tokens, so without this the one line written during an attack is the one recording the capability being attacked.
3. **THREE ROW RULES, NOT ONE** (PD-07). v7.0 filtered at the `places` level only. A place accumulates visits across trips by design, so a place correctly published because it is on the shared trip carries every other trip's visits with it — `fushimi-inari` holds 28 visits across four trips, exactly ONE of them on the shared `autumn-crossing`, and one of the other 27 carries a note. shareNotes is true on that trip, so the note filter does not save it, and BOTH of v7.0's named legs pass while it leaks. The rules: places = distinct places having a visit on THIS trip; visits within a published place = only that place's visits whose trip_id is the shared trip; photos and walks = trip_id.
4. **THE CAPABILITY HEADERS ARE ASSERTED HERE, FROM THE ROUTE TABLE** (PD-09). v7.0 wired DEC-51 into R3 and builds the route here, and R8's file list never touched that middleware — while DEC-51's own evidence paragraph names this route as the motivating case. It matters more here than anywhere: `/l/{token}` carries no Authorization header, so RFC 9111 §3.5's shared-cache prohibition — the thing silently protecting `GET /v1/logbook` — does not reach it, and a 200 with an ETag and no Cache-Control is heuristically cacheable by any intermediary. After 'Stop sharing' a cached envelope keeps handing out live media capabilities, which unbounds the window DEC-44 shrank to two minutes. Measured: NO response on the live server sets Cache-Control at all.
5. **THE PUBLIC READ GETS ITS OWN LIMITER AND ITS OWN NUMBER** (PD-09). Under v7.0's `!Auth` derivation it would inherit `AUTH_RATE_LIMIT_PER_MIN` — a CREDENTIAL budget of 10/min — from the SAME bucket instance as register and sign-in, so one person browsing a shared trip locks everybody out of signing in. routes.go:17-18 already predicted this day in its own words: 'The day an unauthenticated route arrives that is not a credential attempt, this becomes a sixth field rather than a derivation.' **AND THE HONEST SENTENCE GOES IN THE FILE**: this limit is unenforceable behind a proxy until ClientKey learns X-Forwarded-For, and Caddy is deferred to next_slice — the same sentence ratelimit.go already carries.
6. **REVOKED AND UNKNOWN DO THE SAME WORK, NOT MERELY THE SAME BYTES** (PD-12). DEC-10 says 'the SAME 404 WITH THE SAME WORK DONE'; v7.0 carried only 'byte-identical'. A handler that returns early on 'no row' but, for a revoked row, resolves the trip, checks three flags and mints URLs is byte-identical and still a clean oracle for 'this token was once real' — which DEC-67's revocation-history design makes worth attacking. Select the row regardless of `revoked_at` and decide afterwards, so the lookup is the only branch.
7. THE ALLOWLIST GUARD IS STRUCTURAL: parse, walk, assert the key set at every level EQUALS the allowlist. That is what lets a city's centre stay visible — the assertion becomes 'the only `lat` in this document is under cities[].centre', which a substring search cannot express.
8. TWO MINT SURFACES. When sharePhotos is false a signed URL must not be MINTED AT ALL — not minted and withheld — because a minted URL is a live capability whether or not it reaches the response. And every minted URL uses the PUBLIC TTL, which OE-15's replacement leg asserts by call site rather than by comparing the two numbers.
9. sharePhotos off removes `photos` entirely. shareNotes off strips Visit.note AND Photo.caption. shareCoordinates off strips Place.coordinates, Photo.coordinates, Photo.accuracyMetres AND Walk.points; the city CENTRE stays, because it is coarse and it is what a map opens on with no pins.
10. **THE FIFTEEN-MINUTE WINDOW HAS NO REFRESH PATH AND NO LEGIBLE FAILURE, AND ONE SENTENCE FIXES THE FIRST** (DEC-84, STO-MAJ-9). The envelope embeds URLs and carries `Cache-Control: no-store`; `POST /v1/media/mint` is authenticated, so an unauthenticated reader has no way to re-mint. Fifteen minutes is therefore a HARD WALL from the moment the envelope was generated, not a rolling window, and whoever renders the share page must re-GET `/l/{token}` to refresh them. That sentence goes in this step's own text. THE SECOND HALF IS A CLIENT ITEM AND IT IS WORSE THAN INVISIBLE: `log_image.dart` draws a silent plate on any image error, and the client's own record justifies that silence with 'today every asset is bundled and declared, so a failure plate means a build defect rather than something a user can act on'. A presigned URL makes that premise false — expiry is routine and user-actionable — so the 'drawn, not spoken' decision needs re-examining, in the same CLIENT-PREREQUISITES pass as DEC-47's ImageProvider, because both are about the client learning that a picture can now fail for a reason a user can act on.
11. **AND WHAT THE EMBEDDED URL IS** (STO-MIN-12): a pure bearer capability, 394 characters, with unlimited replay and unsigned request headers such as `Range` accepted. Twelve of them is roughly 4.7 kB of JSON on top of the read. That is what makes `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer` load-bearing rather than hygiene — it is what keeps the capability out of the next site's logs — and it is why item 8's 'not minted at all' rule is about minting and not about the response body.
steps.acceptance_check:
```bash
make check && make slice && make seed   # NOT `seed && check && slice` — see DEC-92 and R4

# the whole surface is live in the CONTAINER, not just in go test
scripts/slice-arc.sh arc

# the token never reaches the log — AND the log is not simply empty
make logs | grep -c '/l/\[redacted\]'   # -> non-zero: the positive control
make logs | grep -c 'mnpqrstuvwxy'        # -> 0

# the capability response is not cacheable by an intermediary (PD-09)
curl -sSi http://127.0.0.1:8080/l/mnpqrstuvwxy | grep -iE 'cache-control|referrer-policy'
#   -> Cache-Control: no-store, private
#   -> Referrer-Policy: no-referrer

# a published place carries one trip's visits (PD-07)
curl -sS http://127.0.0.1:8080/l/mnpqrstuvwxy | \
  jq '[.places[] | select(.id=="fushimi-inari") | .visits | length]'   # -> [1], not [28]
```
HOW IT CAN FAIL: as above. The FIRST grep is what makes the second one evidence — a redaction check with no positive control passes against a log that was never written. The jq line answers `[28]` under the defect PD-07 names, and every key in that document is on the allowlist, which is why the structural key walk cannot substitute for it.
steps.verified_by: Six mutations, their diffs, their reds, and for each one WHICH leg went red — because two of them redden exactly one leg and that is the evidence the other legs are not doing the same job twice. The golden files, plus the leg asserting the golden IS the allowlist so that a golden regenerated to match a mistake reddens too. docs/BEFORE-A-PUBLIC-DEPLOY.md, unticked and dated.
steps.commit: feat(httpapi): the public read, against an allowlist rather than a list of things to hide

next_slice.rule: agent-graph-spec-V4 §1. This plan is eight steps, so what comes after is NAMED and not planned. The next plan is written by somebody who has seen R1-R8 run, with them as entry_state.
next_slice.what_it_is: CADDY AND THE PROXY HOP, and it is a slice rather than a chore because it is the first time a request in this system passes through something before reaching the API.
next_slice.why_it_is_first_next: httpx.ClientKey keys on RemoteAddr. That is correct for a direct connection and wrong the moment a proxy appears, at which point every request arrives from the proxy's address and the rate limiter is ONE BUCKET FOR THE WHOLE INTERNET — in front of an unauthenticated Argon2 surface costing 64 MiB per attempt and a public share read. It has been deferred twice, by the slice and by this plan, and it is now the largest single thing standing between this stack and anything a second machine can reach. The leg that settles it exists nowhere: two different X-Forwarded-For values behind ONE RemoteAddr, and separate buckets.
what_else_is_in_it: The fourth compose service, its two named volumes (without caddy_data and caddy_config, automatic HTTPS re-issues on every restart), and go_backend.md L32 finally satisfied at three services plus the fourth divergence.
DEF-01 and DEF-02: how a physical iPhone reaches the stack, and which hostname the bucket is addressed by.

The `.env.example` / compose / config.Load coverage test — one leg, and the last item on EVIDENCE.md's 'guarded by nothing' list that a single test closes. Delete ARGON2_MAX_CONCURRENT from the compose file today and `make check` stays green while the container refuses to start.
`-sweep-media`: the orphan sweep with its grace window, over four liveness columns rather than one (DEC-46). It has a schedule of nobody.
README, and docs/BEFORE-A-PUBLIC-DEPLOY.md ticked by a human with a device.

`media.Store.Remove` and the sweep together (OE-12). The database lens's carry-forward is the constraint to design against: with DEC-58's four foreign keys at ON DELETE RESTRICT, a single-statement `DELETE FROM media_objects` aborts the whole sweep on the first live object, so the NOT EXISTS across all four columns is load-bearing for the sweep's own liveness and not only for correctness. It is also what reclaims PD-11's refused oversized uploads, which nothing in R1-R8 does.

The three deployment items the security lens listed and correctly declined to action for a loopback stack: `POSTGRES_PASSWORD` defaulting to a literal, `sslmode=disable`, and no `read_only`/`cap_drop`/`no-new-privileges` on the api service — least urgent of the three because stage 2 is already scratch with a numeric non-root user and no shell. They go on the checklist CLAUDE.md calls 'guarded by nothing but a human with a device', beside the iOS manifest flags.

`/healthz`'s unlimited `PingContext` against a pool of 8 (security lens, minor): loopback-bound today, so before anything is published either put it behind the proxy's ACL or give it a separate high-ceiling limiter — and do not fold it into the auth bucket.

`Params.check`'s missing UPPER bounds on Argon2 memory and time (security lens, minor). The gate counts slots rather than bytes, so a stored PHC encoding with `m=4194304` would allocate 4 GiB inside one slot and the ceiling the gate exists to provide would not be a memory ceiling. Only this build's own Hash writes those rows, which is why it is minor — and DEC-21's deferred tuning is exactly the moment somebody edits those numbers by hand.

`X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff` on everything `WriteJSON` writes (security lens, minor). It is currently present only on the mux's rewritten 404/405, because stdlib `http.Error` set it before `envelopeWriter` took over — so it is on the responses nobody chose it for and absent from every response the app writes deliberately. One line, or one small `httpx.SecurityHeaders()` middleware, which is also where PD-09's headers could land if the route-table approach proves awkward.

DEF-07's media backup and DEF-08's two orphan classes, which arrive together because the sweep is what reclaims one of them and `mc mirror` is what protects the other. The ORDER when both land is already fixed by DEC-92: bucket first, database second.

The healthcheck's own two unwritten facts (OPS-MIN-13): `/healthz` is a LIVENESS probe answering a READINESS question — its answer is about the connection pool rather than about whether the API can serve, and both inversions were observed in a single run — and NOTHING CONSUMES `unhealthy`. Compose does not restart on it and no orchestrator is planned, so the probe's only real consumer is `--wait` at deploy time and an unhealthy container keeps taking traffic indefinitely. One comment in the compose file, in the voice the pg_isready block already uses; restart-on-unhealthy is a deliberate seventh-service conversation rather than a default.
next_slice.and_after_that: The large seed generator — internal/seed.Generate, 50,000 photographs across three travellers — and DEC-70's index question at a size where the planner's answer means something. It is deliberately LAST rather than first: the catalog leg already proves every FK child column leads an index, which is the claim that is true at any size, and the generator answers a different question that nothing is currently asking. It is also the only thing left that would make DEF-03's timeout numbers measurable.

risks.risk: R2 is the largest single increase in this project's dependency footprint and it lands in one commit. Sixteen new modules against a repository that has had twenty in total, into a package that signs capabilities.
risks.mitigation: Measured before adoption rather than after: minio-go v7.3.0 declares exactly `go 1.25.0`, tidy leaves the directive alone, build and vet exit 0. The command is in base.measured. The shipped set — as opposed to the module graph — is re-derived from the binary with `go version -m bin/api` once R2 lands, because `go list -m all` reports 235 and that number would be quoted wrongly by the next reader.

risks.risk: THE SHARPEST THING IN R2: `PresignedPutObject` and `Presign` both FAIL OPEN. Reach for either and no checksum is signed, the upload succeeds, the commit's HEAD succeeds, and the address space is poisoned by any client that lies. It looks correct through the whole of development because MinIO is a forgiving verifier.
risks.mitigation: A grep that CAN fail, in the definition of done. The checksum leg against a PINNED MinIO tag. And — this is the part that makes it evidence — the INTERMEDIATE RED is recorded: implement with PresignedPutObject first, watch the bucket return 200 for the wrong bytes, then sign the checksum. A leg written after the correct implementation cannot say it would have caught this.

risks.risk: R4's round-trip leg is the strongest leg in the plan and it is also the one most likely to be weakened rather than satisfied. Its first red will be an enormous cmp.Diff across thirty keys, six ORDER BYs and a jsonb unnest, and the tempting response is to narrow it to the fields that pass.
risks.mitigation: Paste the whole first red into EVIDENCE.md before fixing anything. It is the inventory of what had never been tested, and it is worth more as a record than as a to-do list. The per-field legs underneath it — the visits ordering, the date rendering — exist because the round trip cannot say WHICH thing broke, not so that the round trip can be replaced by them.

risks.risk: R6's statement-order defect and R7's unordered-SELECT defect are both the kind that pass a single green run. The refile mutation in particular can return the right row by luck.
risks.mitigation: `-count=10` on the refile legs and the FAILURE RATE recorded rather than a single red — the same discipline DEC-06's snapshot proof already needs, and the DBA's own measurement (1 of 8 unlocked writers succeeding) is the reason it is not paranoia.

risks.risk: THE FORMAT VERSION. Nothing in R1-R8 is blocked by it and everything after R8 is. The server emits 2, the client accepts only 1, exactly, and the client has no HTTP path at all — apiBaseUrlProvider throws by design and logbookProvider.build() is synchronous by decision.
risks.mitigation: open_rulings[1], docs/CLIENT-PREREQUISITES.md as R1's first item, and a statement in CLAUDE.md that GET /v1/logbook's document is currently unreadable by the client it was written for. It is written as a fact rather than as a risk because it is not a probability — it is the present state.

risks.risk: R8 is the one step where a defect is a privacy leak, and its two leak surfaces are of different kinds: an allowlist a key-walk can check, and an HMAC that must not be computed at all.
risks.mitigation: docs/PUBLIC-ENVELOPE.md written in R5 by somebody not holding the handler. The row-filter leg the key walk cannot substitute for. And the mint leg counting HMAC calls through an instrumented store — because an assertion about the response body is structurally unable to see a URL that was minted and dropped.

risks.risk: DEC-31's whole-log read has never been tested at whole-log size. The slice plan said so in terms and forbade the re-plan from treating the slice as evidence for it.
risks.mitigation: R4 is the first step that can measure it, and its acceptance check records the response size and the time. The performance lens is required for exactly this reason and has not run.

risks.risk: The client work this plan discovers is substantial and this plan cannot do any of it: a sign-in screen that does not exist, DEC-45's seventh dependency, four sentences of copy, an ImageProvider keyed by object id, an async seam through roughly thirty providers, a format bump, and — new — an app with no bundled imagery at all, because wipe/mock-data deleted assets/imagery/ and pubspec.yaml declares no assets.
risks.mitigation: docs/CLIENT-PREREQUISITES.md, created in R1 and appended to by every later step, written for somebody who has not read this repository. It separates code from design from dependency-conversation from what merely becomes available.

risks.risk: `make slice` is run by nobody but a human. There is no CI, `make check` is deliberately fast and Docker-free, and the phases that need a daemon are opt-in — so the arc's evidence is only as fresh as the last time somebody ran it.
risks.mitigation: Unchanged and unmitigated, and said out loud rather than left for a green file to imply otherwise. PD-04 at least keeps the arc in step with the routes, which is the failure this actually causes.

risks.risk: R1 is trivial in size and irreversible in one direction. If the client's `main` branch is deleted or force-pushed before R1 lands, the two photographs are gone and every digest in this document stops being reproducible.
risks.mitigation: R1 is first, and its `why_first` says that this is the reason rather than sequencing. It is the shortest step in the plan; there is no version of this work in which doing it later is better.

risks.risk: ALL SEVEN REQUIRED LENSES HAVE RUN, AND THAT IS THE NEW RISK RATHER THAN THE OLD ONE BEING GONE. None of the seven has read v7.2 — the two that produced v7.1 read v7.0 and the other five read v7.1 — so none has seen R1's new shape, DEC-89's pointer contract, the fourth migration, or the reordered acceptance checks. Ninety-three findings is also ninety-three chances for a fix to be believed rather than made — §6.2's sharpest incident, and this revision has already produced one instance of it (SEC-MAJ-4 was landed at v7.1 and corrected at v7.2 by a different lens).
risks.mitigation: §6.2's FixVerifier, on all ninety-three, and it is a different node from this one. Every entry carries `landed_in` so a verifier can open the location rather than reading an intention, eight are labelled CARRIED-NOT-FIXED so a deferral is graded as a deferral, and the one DECLINED entry carries `why_declined` — because a decline a verifier grades as a fix is worse than a defect on a list. What is NOT mitigated: nothing has read v7.2, and the honest place to say so is here.

risks.risk: THE PATTERN IN THE THREE SELF-CORRECTIONS IS THE REAL RISK, and it is not that v7.0 was careless. All three defects were in things v7.0 wrote CONFIDENTLY and in detail: a mutation with a predicted red, a proof method quoted from a ruling, a hash with the command beside it. A plan that writes its proofs out in full is easier to check and NOT more likely to be right.
risks.mitigation: Every mutation in v7.1 that predicts a specific red says which OTHER leg must stay green — a pair rather than a single assertion, because 'this reddens' is satisfiable by a mutation that breaks everything. And three of the database lens's findings were RE-EXECUTED here before adoption rather than carried, which is how PD-13 was found: it is not in either lens report.

risks.risk: PD-09 gives the public read a rate limit that DOES NOT BIND behind a proxy, and Caddy is deferred for the second time. So R8 ships a control whose evidence is loopback-only, in front of the one route a stranger can reach.
risks.mitigation: Stated in R8's own file text rather than only here, in the same words `ratelimit.go` already carries. It is RULE-05's second half and the human is asked to confirm the deferral knowing that it now weakens a control this plan is adding rather than merely postponing one.

risks.risk: RULE-07 WAS a blocker with no owner and is CLOSED: DEC-84 fixes `S3_PRESIGN_TTL_PUBLIC` at fifteen minutes. What is left is not a risk in the plan but a property of the number: it is sized for a consumer that does not exist, because a rendered share page is out of scope.
risks.mitigation: Recorded as PROVISIONAL in the same tier as the Argon2 parameters and DefaultSessionTTL — asserted as a value so it cannot move unnoticed, with nothing claiming it is the right value. OE-15's replacement leg is MANDATED by the ruling and written out in R2: assert WHICH TTL each call site uses, with a mutation swapping them. And the honest sentence goes into the copy rather than being implied — stopping a share stops new links at once, and a photograph already loaded may keep working for up to fifteen minutes.

risks.risk: Ruling DEC-82 has migration 0002 REWRITE rows a user may have deliberately set. The database lens called it 'a privacy-shaped call' before the ruling settled it.
risks.mitigation: The ruling's reasoning is that those rows carry a server default the client never had, so they are wrong data rather than a choice — and R4's seed makes it moot for seeded rows. What is NOT mitigated is the general case, and the safety lens has not run. It is named in that lens's row as scope that GREW at v7.1.

risks.risk: R1 IS NOW THE LARGEST STEP IN THE PLAN AND IT WAS THE SMALLEST. Nine items, eight of them changes to code that is already running and answering requests, in one commit — a wire contract, a log format, a compression middleware, three timeout bounds, a new status code path, four log fields, three scans and a migration. The obvious failure is that a reviewer approves it as a unit because it is too large to review as parts.
risks.mitigation: It is NOT split, and the reason is in execution.mode rather than only here: every one of the nine changes what the RUNNING BUILD does, and each needs its arc assertion added against a container that already answers, so reviewing them separately means nine reviews of a stack that is mid-change. What makes it reviewable instead is that ELEVEN legs are written out in full with their expected reds, and every mutation names the OTHER leg that must stay green — a pair rather than a single assertion. The `curl` half of the acceptance check is the one that matters: it reproduces the shipped defect from OUTSIDE the test binary, before and after.

risks.risk: DEC-89's POINTER CONTRACT IS A WIRE CHANGE AND THE CLIENT HAS NOT MADE IT. The server will start treating an omitted field as 'leave alone', which is what the client's controls already assume — but nothing on the client side asserts that its write bodies omit rather than send zero values, and `json_serializable` emits explicit nulls for nullable fields by default. A body carrying `"cityIds": null` is not the same as an omitted key, and the server must decide which it is.
risks.mitigation: The contract is stated in both directions and the ambiguity is named rather than left: absent means leave alone; an explicit `null` on a nullable field means CLEAR it; and `visits: []` is refused with a 422 until a control exists that issues it (SAF-MAJ-4). CLIENT-PREREQUISITES carries the encoder-side requirement. The residual is real: nobody has run the client's encoder against the new server, and the first thing that would find it is the client phase rather than anything in R1-R8.

risks.risk: THE TWO LENSES DISAGREED ABOUT WHETHER PRESIGNING TOUCHES THE NETWORK, and the plan now depends on the resolution being right. The storage lens measured `PresignHeader` against a missing bucket returning an error; DEC-98 and the operations lens report that it succeeds and the failure surfaces on the phone. If the resolution (cold cache versus warm) is wrong, then either R3's 'presigning is a local HMAC' is false or DEC-98's motivating failure mode does not exist.
risks.mitigation: The resolution is written into R2's own text rather than into a footnote, with both measurements quoted and the precondition that separates them named. AND IT DOES NOT MATTER TO THE FIX: `EnsureBucket` at boot is correct under both readings — it makes the bucket exist, and it warms the region cache — so the plan does not rest on the resolution being right. That is the honest reason to record the disagreement rather than adjudicate it.

risks.risk: NINETEEN RULINGS WENT UNREAD BETWEEN TWO REVISIONS WHILE THE GATE THAT EXISTS TO CATCH EXACTLY THAT REPORTED THE STAMP AND NOTHING ELSE. The stamp check worked — it was RED at d781d29 — and it caught the field, not the reading. A future revision can re-run the hash, correct the two numbers, and still not open the file.
risks.mitigation: Three new fields on the stamp — count, first and last — so a prose sentence saying THIRTY-TWO beside a correct hash is now a gate failure rather than a lens finding. It is a smaller fix than it should be and it is stated as such: nothing mechanical can prove a human or an agent READ nineteen rulings, and the only real defence is that the ruling ids are now cited from the steps that implement them, so an unread ruling is a ruling nothing cites.

open_rulings.severity: CLOSED at v7.1 by ruling DEC-76
open_rulings.question: The server stamps `"version": 2` and refuses anything else; the client refuses anything but 1, exactly. Which side moves?
open_rulings.resolution: RULED: the CLIENT bumps `logbookFormatVersion` to 2. No server change. The ruling justifies it on the client's own terms rather than to match the server — `Photo.asset` and the three `coverAsset` fields change MEANING from a bundled path to an object id, and the client's own rule is to move the version when an old file's meaning changes. AND IT ADDS THE ARGUMENT v7.0 DID NOT HAVE, which is what makes the bump safe: under DEC-34 a cache the client cannot read is DELETED AND RE-FETCHED, not quarantined, so a version bump costs one refetch where against a file-as-record it would have cost the log. Recorded as the first item in docs/CLIENT-PREREQUISITES.md and it must land before the first real request.

open_rulings.severity: CLOSED at v7.1 by ruling DEC-77, and already executed at 7b47bee
open_rulings.question: May 1,084,768 bytes of PNG be committed to this Go repository?
open_rulings.resolution: RULED and DONE. Captured at `internal/logbook/testdata/imagery/` — NOT the `internal/media/testdata/` path v7.0 invented, which is why v7.0's decision is deleted (OE-14) rather than kept alongside. They are test data rather than app assets: the client ships no imagery now, and these exist so `make seed` can put real bytes in the bucket and the content addresses in this plan stay true.

open_rulings.severity: minor, OPEN — WIDENED at v7.2: it now touches an APPROVED artefact in two places, not one
open_rulings.question: `GET /v1/me` is deleted (OE-7) because it has no caller, and ruling DEC-86 closes `POST /v1/auth/register` after the first traveller. Does GATE-L12's clearance survive either? The clearance covers six sequence diagrams including `register`, and its own KNOWN-OPEN list names 'the register and sign-in request bodies'.
open_rulings.recommendation: Ratify both, but say so explicitly rather than letting it be inferred. DEC-86 is the sharper of the two, because it changes an error state on a diagram whose request body the approver had already flagged as open — a second registration now answers 409 for a reason the diagram does not carry. DEC-91's additive `shared` field is judged NOT material and is recorded as judged rather than left silent.
open_rulings.why_it_needs_a_human: An approval with no scope is the same defect wearing a tick, and only the approver can say whether a change is material. The clearance's own note says it: 'If the diagrams change materially, this clearance does not carry over — re-approve.'

open_rulings.severity: CLOSED at v7.1 by ruling DEC-78
open_rulings.question: The database service is `postgres` in the shipped compose file and `db` in v6's S22. CLAUDE.md asked the re-plan to settle it.
open_rulings.resolution: RULED: `postgres` everywhere. It is what is running and what `DATABASE_URL` names.

open_rulings.severity: confirm-or-object, OPEN — NARROWED at v7.2: its compression half is closed by ruling DEC-94
open_rulings.question: Caddy, the `.env.example`/`config.Load` coverage leg, and the media sweep stay outside these eight steps.
open_rulings.recommendation: Accept, and note what changed. THE COMPRESSION HALF IS NO LONGER BLOCKING: v7.1 leaned on Caddy for gzip and DEC-94 puts it in the Go server instead, with the reason that Caddy is deferred and the Go server IS the edge today — measured, `GET /v1/logbook` answers 200 with a valid ETag and a body cut mid-token, and gzip level 1 takes the fixture from 99,271 to 6,806 bytes in 0.3 ms. WHAT REMAINS OPEN IS THE PROXY HOP AND IT IS UNCHANGED: the public read's rate limit is UNENFORCEABLE behind a proxy until `ClientKey` learns X-Forwarded-For, so PD-09's number does not bind on the day this stack goes behind anything. And the sweep's absence is load-bearing for two orphan classes, now measured and written into DEF-08.
open_rulings.why_it_needs_a_human: Deferring the same thing twice is how it becomes permanent, and this is still the second deferral for Caddy rather than a third — v7.2 does not defer it again, it takes one of the three things riding on it out and does it here. open_rulings.severity: CLOSED at v7.2 by ruling DEC-84
open_rulings.question: What is `S3_PRESIGN_TTL_PUBLIC`? DEC-47 makes it 'THE HONEST REVOCATION WINDOW' that D3's and H1's copy must be written against; the private one is ~2 minutes and the public one is described only as 'longer'.
open_rulings.what_is_already_true: It is the single number that decides how long 'Stop sharing' is a lie, and it is the number four sentences of client copy (DEC-56) will be written against. It cannot be derived: it is a trade between a share page that stays readable below the fold and a revocation that bites. There is no page yet — a rendered share page is out of scope — so the honest framing is that this number is sized for a consumer that does not exist.
open_rulings.recommendation: Name a number and record that it is provisional, in the same tier as the Argon2 parameters and DefaultSessionTTL: asserted as a value so it cannot move unnoticed, with nothing claiming it is the right value. Fifteen minutes is defensible against a page nobody has built; so is two. What is not defensible is 'longer'.
open_rulings.why_it_needs_a_human: DEC-44 shrank the private window deliberately so that H1's plain sentence would be true enough to keep. This is the same call for the public side and it belongs to whoever writes that sentence.
open_rulings.resolution: RULED: `S3_PRESIGN_TTL_PUBLIC = 15m`, and it IS the revocation window the copy must be written against. `S3_PRESIGN_TTL_PRIVATE` stays short (~2m, DEC-44). THE RULING ALSO ORDERS THE LEG THIS PLAN HAD ALREADY DELETED WITHOUT SEEING IT: 'R2's TTL leg was DELETED at v7.1 for being unfalsifiable (it compared the two values to each other); the replacement must assert the PUBLIC path uses the PUBLIC value — a handler reaching for the private one is the defect, and it would have reddened nothing.' So OE-15's deletion stands and its replacement is MANDATED, written out in R2's test_strategy with a mutation that swaps them. AND THE HONEST SENTENCE IS THE RULING'S OWN, for PD-16's class (ii): stopping a share stops new links at once, and a photograph already loaded may keep working for up to fifteen minutes. R2 is no longer blocked.

open_rulings.severity: CLOSED at v7.2 by ruling DEC-85
open_rulings.question: DEC-10 stores the share token in PLAINTEXT. Session tokens are hashed, with a whole argued section explaining why the hash is of the raw bytes. There is no parallel argument for share tokens anywhere in CLAUDE.md or in this plan. Is plaintext still the ruling?
open_rulings.what_is_already_true: Two things have changed since DEC-10 was ruled. PD-08 measured the same token landing in the access log in plaintext — `"path":"/l/CAPABILITY7XY"` — so a live capability is currently written to disk twice, in the database and in the log. And DEC-67's history design keeps every revoked row forever, so a database dump holds every capability ever issued, live and dead, in the clear.
open_rulings.recommendation: Hashing costs the revocation-history design NOTHING: store `sha256(token)` and keep the `revoked_at` row exactly as DEC-67 has it. What it costs is `Trip.shareLinkId` round-tripping — DEC-10's actual reason for plaintext, which is that the client displays the link it minted. But the CLIENT mints the token, so the client already holds it; the server needs to recognise it, not to reproduce it. That is worth re-examining rather than inheriting.
open_rulings.why_it_needs_a_human: DEC-10 is a ruling with a stated reason, and the reason may still hold for a case I cannot see. PD-08 fixes the log; it does not fix the dump.
open_rulings.resolution: RULED: share tokens are HASHED at rest and DEC-10's plaintext half is REVERSED. `share_links.token_hash bytea`, sha256 of the raw token, constant-time compared — the shape `sessions` already uses — and `share_links_token_key` becomes a unique index on the hash. That is migration 0004 and it is why the migration count moves to four. THE COST IS REAL AND THE RULING NAMES IT: the server can no longer emit `Trip.shareLinkId`. THE CLIENT-FIDELITY LENS THEN MEASURED THAT THE COST IS LARGER THAN THE RULING'S OWN ESTIMATE — not restricted to restores at all, because DEC-32's write response is a whole Trip the phone SPLICES into its cache, so an ordinary rename overwrites the local plaintext token with null and leaves both 'Copy link' and 'Stop sharing' inert while the row is un-revoked and `GET /l/{token}` still serves it. DEC-91 is the answer and it lands in R1: emit `shared` as a derived boolean. Read the two rulings together; neither is complete alone.

open_rulings.severity: minor, OPEN — one character, and CHECKED against the nineteen unread rulings rather than assumed
open_rulings.question: DEC-51's allowlist is `^image/(jpeg|png|heic)$`. Should `heic` be in it?
open_rulings.what_is_already_true: Nothing in this system can produce a HEIC. The client's shutter is inert by decision, DEC-41 seeds two PNGs, and the fixture's 284 photographs resolve to two `image/png` objects. `image/jpeg` earns its place independently of any camera: `internal/postgres/schema_test.go:62` seeds shared fixtures with it, so omitting it breaks every leg using that helper. RE-CHECKED AT v7.2 AGAINST DEC-84..DEC-102: none of the nineteen unread rulings touches the allowlist, so this stays open rather than being closed by accident. What DID change around it is DEC-87 — Content-Type is now SIGNED into the PUT from the same validated value the 422 and the CHECK see — so the allowlist now reaches the OBJECT and not only the row, which makes each entry in it worth slightly more and an unused entry worth slightly less.
open_rulings.recommendation: Enumerate DEC-51's list as ruled — this plan does — and narrow it to `^image/(jpeg|png)$` only if you agree. An allowlist entry no code path can create is a format the XSS argument has to cover for nothing.

open_rulings.severity: CLOSED at v7.2 by ruling DEC-86
open_rulings.question: `POST /v1/auth/register` is public and answers 409 on a duplicate — a deliberate, well-argued enumeration surface (an address's availability is a fact a sign-up form must report). Should registration close after the first traveller, or gate on an env-supplied invite?
open_rulings.what_is_already_true: Under single-user registration the 409 is nearly harmless. But the route is also how a stranger gets an authenticated account on a deployed instance — and after `d5be39c` an authenticated account has a 600/min budget, the whole write surface, and from R6 a `DELETE /v1/places/{id}?photos=delete`. The security lens raised it; the plan's own out_of_scope already says invites and roles are out, which is not the same as saying registration is open.
open_rulings.recommendation: Close it after the first traveller, or gate it on an env variable. It is one line and one leg, and it turns 'local-only target' from a deployment posture into something the code enforces. It is NOT scheduled in R1-R8; it belongs with Caddy, in the step where this stack first faces something other than loopback.
open_rulings.why_it_needs_a_human: It changes what the product is. A backend that refuses a second traveller is a single-user backend by construction, which may be exactly right and is not this plan's call.
open_rulings.resolution: RULED: registration refuses once ANY traveller row exists. It is one line and it removes the whole question rather than bounding it. NOTE THE ORACLE SHRINKS RATHER THAN GROWS, which is the part the plan's own recommendation missed: the 409-on-duplicate the security lens flagged as an enumeration surface becomes a 409-on-any-second-registration, which tells an attacker only that the instance is in use — a fact the login page already gives them. IT MOVES INTO SCOPE: v7.1 had it in `next_slice` as 'RULE-10's registration gate, IF THE HUMAN TAKES IT', and the human took it, so it lands in R5 with the other auth work. AND IT COLLIDES WITH R4 AS WRITTEN — see ruling DEC-97, which is the collision's fix and lands in the same revision.

open_rulings.severity: major, OPEN — NEW at v7.2, and it is a DEC-12 decision rather than a patch
open_rulings.question: Every route this plan has not built yet answers `{"code":"not_found"}` — the same word the vocabulary uses for 'that trip is not in your log'. Does the closed twelve-code vocabulary want a THIRTEENTH word for 'this build does not have that route'?
open_rulings.what_is_already_true: Measured live against a server at R1 entry state: `DELETE /v1/trips/{id}` -> `405 {"code":"not_found"}`; `PATCH /v1/me` -> `404 {"code":"not_found"}`; `PUT /v1/places/x` -> `404 {"code":"not_found"}`. TWO CONSEQUENCES AND THE SECOND IS THE BAD ONE. A client build ahead of the server tells the user their trip, place, photograph or walk is GONE, on eighteen routes, and `NotFoundScreen` says exactly that. And `deletePhoto`, `removePlace` and `deleteTrip` all treat an unknown id as SUCCESS by decision — 'the caller asked for that photo to be absent and it is' — so the obvious network mapping (`not_found` -> true) makes a delete against an undeployed route report success, delete nothing, and advance the cache. R5, R6 and R7 each ship deletes, so it is live for the whole rollout rather than a corner. Note also that the status and the code DISAGREE on the 405s: `internal/httpx/mux.go:89` returns the same prebuilt body for both, which is deliberate (VS7 refused `method_not_allowed` under DEC-12) and reads as an accident.
open_rulings.recommendation: THE CLIENT HALF IS NOT OPTIONAL AND IS SCHEDULED REGARDLESS OF THE ANSWER: CLIENT-PREREQUISITES requires the API layer to branch on the HTTP STATUS as well as the code, so a 404 or 405 on a route the client's own table believes in is a DEPLOYMENT MISMATCH and never the delete-succeeded branch. The open question is only whether the server should say so in a word. A thirteenth code is cheap and DEC-12 exists precisely so that it is not cheap to add; the alternative is that the client uses `X-Logbook-Format`, which the server already sends, to say 'this needs a newer server'.
open_rulings.why_it_needs_a_human: DEC-12 closed the vocabulary deliberately and VS7 has already refused one addition. Adding the thirteenth is a decision about the vocabulary, not a patch to a handler, and this plan does not open a closed ruling on its own initiative.

execution.mode: One worker per step, sequential, with a review between steps. R5, R6 and R7 are mutually independent once R4 lands and may be reviewed in any order — but they are not parallel zones, because all three write to internal/httpapi/routes.go and internal/postgres, and `parallel_zones` requires disjoint sole-write paths (§3). AT v7.2 R1 IS THE STEP THAT MOST WANTS SPLITTING AND MUST NOT BE SPLIT: its nine items share one property that is the reason they are one step — every one of them changes what the RUNNING BUILD does, and the arc assertion for each has to be added against a container that already answers. Reviewing them separately would mean nine reviews of a stack that is mid-change.
execution.test_first: MANDATORY, §6.7, and it is inherited from the client's own record rather than imposed: 'Test-first for new behaviour. When tests must come after — porting, integrating generated code — say so and name what gets backfilled.' Every behavioural step above carries its first failing test IN FULL and states what the red must say. A test that passes before the implementation exists is testing something else, and that is discovered now or never.
execution.write_it_and_break_it: §8, EVERY test and not only guards. A test that has never been red has never been shown to work, and a green suite cannot tell the difference. Under test-first this is nearly free — step 2 already ran it red — so the only deliberate breaks needed are for tests written against code that already works, and those are LABELLED backfill.
execution.restore_by_file_copy_never_git_checkout: The client's plans say it, this project's VS2 lost a step's implementation by ignoring it, and six of thirteen mutation results were contaminated. Against an uncommitted tree `git checkout --` no-ops on untracked files and restores tracked ones from the index, so mutations stack and a later red belongs to an earlier one — while the suite keeps going red, which looks exactly like success.
execution.a_mutation_that_did_not_change_the_file: proves nothing. Diff before running, and check the sha256 moved. One mutation in VS6 changed a comment inside a SQL string and left the suite green.
execution.note: Two things this plan asks for that are easy to skip and are the reason the last four steps are trustworthy or not. First, PD-04: the arc grows in the same commit as the route, and the reviewer's first check is `git show --stat` against scripts/slice-arc.sh. Second, the INTERMEDIATE RED in R2 — a leg written after the correct implementation cannot demonstrate that it would have caught the defect, and R2's defect is one that looks correct for the whole of development.

mechanical_invariants.rule: §6.5 — cross-references, counts, ids, step numbering and any re-derived figure are checked by CODE, as a gate. An agent's claim to have re-derived something is not evidence.
checks: Every step id referenced anywhere in this document resolves to a step in `steps`.
No id appears twice across `decisions`, `deferred_decisions`, `deletions`, `open_rulings` and `steps`.
Every `definition_of_done` entry maps to at least one step.
No step touches anything in `out_of_scope` — in particular, no step's `files` list contains a path under /Users/mattmarshall/Documents/Flutter/Travel Log.
No step's `files` list contains the strings `internal/api/`, `internal/rest/`, `internal/store/` or `internal/objects/`. This is the check v6 needed for six revisions and never had.
The route arithmetic in `sequencing.notes[0]` equals the length of `route_table_at_the_end_of_R8`.
Every step has a non-empty `test_strategy`, and every behavioural one contains an actual test body rather than a description of one.
Every acceptance check names how it could fail.

THE RULINGS FILE IS READ, NOT TRUSTED: no plan decision claims a `DEC-` id, every `DEC-` the plan cites resolves to a ruling or to v6's own list, and `base.inputs`' size and sha256 for the rulings file are RECOMPUTED rather than compared to a field. This is the check whose absence let v7.0 certify a stale hash and reuse three ruling ids while the gate reported 0 failures.

Every citation exemption names a LOCATION and carries a reason longer than a sentence, and the exemption register is not itself scanned. THE FIRST DRAFT OF THIS EXEMPTED THE IDS GLOBALLY AND WAS THEREFORE A CHECK THAT COULD NOT FAIL — it passed while two real dangling citations stood in R4's file list. Scoping it to the field found them, and that is recorded because it is the seventh time an artefact check in this project has been wrong about the artefact rather than about the code.

§6.2 COVERAGE: `claimed_fixes` holds exactly one entry per finding in the two lens reports — COUNTED AGAINST THE REPORTS, not against a number written here — and every entry names a location a FixVerifier can open. It caught four entries whose location was the bare word `next_slice`, which is a deferral wearing a fix's clothes; those four now name the exact list index and carry `verdict_expected: CARRIED, NOT FIXED` so a verifier grades them as deferrals.

§6.2 COVERAGE IS COUNTED AGAINST ALL SEVEN LENS REPORTS, NOT TWO. The expected finding-id set is DERIVED positionally from the reports — `{LENS}-{BLO|MAJ|MIN}-{index}` — and `claimed_fixes`' id set must equal it exactly. At v7.1 the check read two reports and passed at 28 entries while five reports and 65 findings sat unread beside it.

EVERY BLOCKER NAMES THE STEP IT LANDS IN, OR IS DECLINED WITH A REASON. Each blocker's claimed_fix carries `landed_in` naming a step id (or `base` / `decisions` / `next_slice`), and a `landed_in` of `DECLINED` requires a `why_declined` longer than a sentence. A blocker that is silently dropped is the failure this plan has already had from the other direction, with nineteen rulings.

NO ACCEPTANCE CHECK TEACHES `make seed` FOLLOWED BY `make slice` ON ONE LINE (DEC-92). Five of the eight steps read `make seed && make check && make slice`, and step A0 of the arc is `docker compose down -v` against the live project. A convention this document got wrong five times in one release needs a command rather than a rule.

`internal/logbook/emit.go` APPEARS IN AT LEAST ONE STEP'S FILE LIST. It appeared in NONE at v7.1, while the definition_of_done carried the rule that every route answering a bare entity goes through an EmitX function — a rule with nowhere to land, which is a different failure from a rule being wrong and is not one a green suite can see.

global_constraints.source: *** PROVENANCE — PLAN-LEVEL NOTE, NOT A CONSTRAINT ***
global_constraints.how_honoured: THE SPEC WAS MISSING FOR FOUR REVISIONS AND HAS BEEN RECOVERED AND VERIFIED. This line stays after the resolution because the next reader should know the check HAPPENED rather than assume it did — an absent note reads identically to a check nobody ran. What happened: `go_backend.md` could not be found at its named path or anywhere under $HOME; every `how_honoured` row below was marked corroborated-but-unverifiable; the human ruled 'proceed — the plan is the record'; the file then resurfaced at `sha256=e546f63d…`; and all 13 spec-sourced quotes were diffed against it mechanically, VERBATIM, with ZERO MISMATCHES. The four unquoted lines L26-L29 turned out to be a heading gap and no constraint was lost. THE UNCERTAINTY RESOLVED IN THE PLAN'S FAVOUR, and it was still worth disclosing while it stood. ONE NARROWING THAT MUST NOT DRIFT: the Trash was never searched — that attempt returned a permissions error misread as an empty result — so 'the Trash was empty' is a claim nobody established and appears nowhere. TWO NOTES from the recovered text: L28 says the deployment files are to run this **on a VPS**, so DEC-21's local-only ruling stands but the pre-deploy checklist is answering a stated REQUIREMENT rather than a precaution; and L12's approval gate is NOT CLEARED — see `sequencing.gate`.

global_constraints.quote: Use Go 1.22 or higher. Follow the Standard Go Project Layout (e.g., `cmd/api/main.go` and `internal/`).
global_constraints.how_honoured: cmd/api/main.go + internal/{config,logging,httpx,auth,logbook,postgres,media,httpapi} (DEC-71, DEC-74). go.mod `go 1.25.0`, which SATISFIES 'or higher'. The floor is a divergence from ruling 4, not from the spec (DEC-27).

global_constraints.quote: Strictly use the native `net/http` multiplexer (`http.ServeMux`). Do not use third-party routers like Chi, Gin, or Gorilla.
global_constraints.how_honoured: One *http.ServeMux built from a declared []Route slice, using method+wildcard patterns. ServeMux does all matching; the slice is a registration source, not a router (DEC-28, forced by the measured absence of pattern enumeration).

global_constraints.quote: Exclusively use `encoding/json` for payload encoding and decoding.
global_constraints.how_honoured: Two functions in internal/httpx are the only importers. DEC-26's jsonb columns marshal through the same package — one choice satisfying two constraints.

global_constraints.quote: Use the standard `database/sql` package exclusively. Do not use GORM, sqlc, or sqlx. Use `_ "github.com/jackc/pgx/v5/stdlib"` solely as a blank import driver.
global_constraints.how_honoured: The blank import appears exactly once, in cmd/api/main.go. Hand-rolled SQL over *sql.DB. Every column is a scalar or jsonb, so no driver-specific type support is ever needed (DEC-26). Photograph bytes never touch the database at all (DEC-36).

global_constraints.quote: Explicitly configure connection pooling in `main.go` using `SetMaxOpenConns()` and `SetMaxIdleConns()`.
global_constraints.how_honoured: Both called explicitly from env, plus lifetimes. Sized together with Argon2's 64 MiB-per-login ceiling — and DEC-36's direct-to-bucket upload exists partly so multi-megabyte transfers never join that contest.

global_constraints.quote: Use the standard `context` package to handle request timeouts and pass request-scoped data.
global_constraints.how_honoured: ReadHeaderTimeout/WriteTimeout, a per-request http.TimeoutHandler whose body IS the JSON envelope (the one response the error-vocabulary sweep cannot see), ctx first on every store and objects method, request-scoped data via unexported context key types.

global_constraints.quote: Write custom validation methods on request structs using standard Go logic and the `regexp` package. No third-party validation libraries.
global_constraints.how_honoured: `Validate() *httpx.Error` on every request struct. Compiled regexps: `idRe = ^[a-z0-9-]{1,64}$` (permissive — it MUST accept `kyoto`), `sha256Re = ^[0-9a-f]{64}$`, emailRe, countryCodeRe. Ranges in plain Go.

global_constraints.quote: Implement opaque session tokens. Generate 32-byte strings via `crypto/rand`, hash them with `crypto/sha256`, and store the hashes in PostgreSQL.
global_constraints.how_honoured: crypto/rand 32 bytes -> base64.RawURLEncoding (43 chars) -> sha256 of the RAW bytes as bytea, compared with subtle.ConstantTimeCompare. THREE TOKEN KINDS, THREE TREATMENTS, and CLAUDE.md states the boundary so they are never conflated: SESSION tokens are HASHED (this line); SHARE tokens are PLAINTEXT so `Trip.shareLinkId` round-trips (DEC-10); MEDIA access is a SIGNED, EXPIRING URL and is stored nowhere (DEC-37).

global_constraints.quote: Use the standard `log/slog` package for structured JSON logging.
global_constraints.how_honoured: slog JSON, level from env, with TWO redactors: an attr redactor (token, passphrase, authorization) and a URL-path redactor rewriting `/l/{token}` to `/l/[redacted]`, because DEC-10 puts a live capability in the request line. A leg asserts both.

global_constraints.quote: Read all configuration (DB DSN, ports) strictly via `os.Getenv()`. No third-party config managers in the Go code.
global_constraints.how_honoured: internal/config is the only importer of os.Getenv, asserted by grep. One Load() reporting every missing or invalid var at once. Bucket endpoint, region, credentials and presign lifetime join it — which is what makes MinIO-vs-S3 configuration rather than code.

global_constraints.quote: Write a multi-stage `Dockerfile`. Stage 1 must use `golang:1.22` for the build, and Stage 2 must copy the statically linked binary into a minimal `scratch` image.
global_constraints.how_honoured: Stage 2 is `scratch` exactly as mandated. Stage 1 is `golang:1.26` — DIVERGENCE 1 (DEC-09), now doubly forced: a golang:1.22 stage could not compile a module whose floor is 1.25.0. NOTE scratch now matters more: DEC-36 makes outbound HTTPS to the bucket a real code path, so the CA bundle is load-bearing rather than precautionary.

global_constraints.quote: Write a `docker-compose.yml` defining three services: the Go API, a PostgreSQL database (with persistent volume mapping), and a Caddy reverse proxy for automatic HTTPS.
global_constraints.how_honoured: FOUR services — DIVERGENCE 3 (DEC-39), and unlike DEC-27 this one IS from the spec. api, db (named volume `pgdata`), caddy (with caddy_data/caddy_config, without which automatic HTTPS re-issues on every restart into a Let's Encrypt rate limit), and minio. The fourth is LOCAL ONLY: a public deploy against real S3 has exactly the three the spec names.

global_constraints.quote: Wait for my approval on the diagrams before proceeding to Phase 2.
global_constraints.how_honoured:
*** NOT SATISFIED. THIS IS THE ONE OPEN GATE IN THE PLAN. *** v4 said 'SATISFIED. Phase 1's diagrams were approved and the human has issued rulings off them across three rounds.' THAT WAS WRONG, and it is the plan's most consequential self-inflicted error: the human ruled on DECISIONS put to them in prose and never saw a diagram. The Phase 1 diagrams were produced before a context compaction, were never written to disk, and have never been shown to anybody. Rulings on decisions are not approval of artefacts nobody has seen.
A prior critique raised this (SF14c) and the fix did not land — the SECOND instance of a finding cited as fixed while its substance was untouched, after V4-B1. That pattern is why this revision emits `claimed_fixes` for a fresh verifier instead of certifying its own work.
WHAT IS DONE ABOUT IT: the word 'approved' is struck from every description of the Phase 1 artefacts; `sequencing.gate` states the stop, quoting L12, positioned before any Phase 2 work; S02's header records the diagrams as UNAPPROVED, dated; and the changelog records that the gate was skipped and what caught it. No revision may describe them as approved until a human says so.

global_constraints.quote: There is no loading state because there is no frame in which the log is unknown.
global_constraints.how_honoured: DEC-31. The cache is read before `runApp` exactly as the log is today, `logbookProvider` stays synchronous, and no screen grows a loading state. This sentence is the reason the read path is one whole-log endpoint and not a set of per-screen fetches.

global_constraints.quote: A file carrying anything else is refused rather than guessed at.
global_constraints.how_honoured: DEC-40 moves the emitted version to 2 because `Photo.asset` changes meaning — cheap now because nothing has shipped. And the rule for afterwards is recorded: once a client build exists, a meaning change goes in the PATH, because a cache that refuses and re-fetches LOOPS where a record that quarantines merely stops.

global_constraints.quote: …three services: the Go API, a PostgreSQL database (with persistent volume mapping)…
global_constraints.how_honoured: RESTATED AT v7.1, because the count moves in this plan. The slice shipped TWO services and recorded Caddy as deferred rather than declined. R2 brings MinIO, so the stack is THREE — but not the three L32 names: it is api, postgres and minio, with Caddy still absent. That is divergence 3 (DEC-39) plus a standing deferral, and both are named rather than netted off against each other. `next_slice` owns Caddy and RULE-05 asks the human to confirm the second deferral knowing it now weakens PD-09's rate limit rather than merely postponing TLS.

global_constraints.how_honoured: UNCHANGED, and v7.1 finally gives it its missing regexp: PD-10 enumerates `^image/(jpeg|png|heic)$` in `internal/logbook/validate.go` beside `idPattern` and `assetPattern`. v7.0 named the constraint and deferred the list to the worker, which is why the schema half could not be written and 0001's placeholder had been waiting since VS4.

claimed_fixes_note: §6.2: THE PLANNER DOES NOT GRADE ITS OWN FIXES. NINETY-THREE entries, one per finding across ALL SEVEN lens reports — v7.1 had twenty-eight, counted against two reports, while five reports and sixty-five findings sat unread beside it, and the gate passed. Every entry names the field a FixVerifier can open rather than describing an intention, and every entry carries `landed_in`: a step id, or `base` / `decisions` / `next_slice`, or `DECLINED`. TWENTY-ONE ARE BLOCKERS AND ALL TWENTY-ONE LAND IN A STEP. EXACTLY ONE ENTRY IS DECLINED — SAF-MAJ-7, the name-confirmation gate on `DELETE /v1/trips/{id}` — and it carries `why_declined` as well as `verdict_expected`, because a decline that a verifier grades as a fix is worse than a defect on a list. EIGHT ARE HONEST 'CARRIED, NOT FIXED' (OPS-MIN-13, PERF-MIN-10, SEC-MIN-9, SEC-MIN-11, SEC-MIN-12, SEC-MIN-13, STO-MAJ-8, STO-MIN-13) and say so in their own text — those are the ones to check hardest, because 'carried to next_slice' is the shape a deferral takes when it is really an omission. ONE (SEC-MAJ-6) was fixed in CODE rather than in the plan, at `d5be39c`. AND TWO ARE THE INTERESTING KIND: SEC-MAJ-4 was LANDED AT v7.1 AND THEN CORRECTED AT v7.2 BY A DIFFERENT LENS — the control survives and the sentence describing it did not — and SEC-MAJ-8's namespace split held while the failure it was written for recurred, because a stamp check catches a stale field and nothing catches a stale reading. A `partial` or `absent` verdict on any of the ninety-three outranks the original finding, because the record now says the defect is handled.
